final_text:
**Short answer:** I can't pin a denial reason code on this claim, and the model doesn't predict one. The claim scores as low risk.

**Score:** The model gives claim 1241554 (outpatient, HCPCS 99408, principal diagnosis J02.9) a 3.2% denial probability. The validation average is 18.1%, so this is about 15 points below average. The denial label in this project is synthetic. It was built from risk rules, so this is the probability of that constructed label and not of a real payer decision.

**Why it's low:** The billed code drives most of the score. HCPCS 99408 cuts the odds of denial by about 75%. Provider identifiers each lower the odds slightly. Nothing pushes the score up by more than a small amount.

**Most plausible code, with caveats:**
- **CARC 11** (the diagnosis doesn't support the procedure) is the only code that fits at all. My own reading is that 99408 is an alcohol or substance screening service, and a throat-infection diagnosis doesn't obviously match it. That reading is my background knowledge, and the policy search returned nothing on 99408.
- The model doesn't show this mismatch as a risk driver, so I can't confirm a rule fired.
- CARCs 16, 18, 181 and 197 have no supporting evidence here.

The model outputs only a denial probability and no reason code. Any CARC attached to this claim would be illustrative.
